text: Shanice Lorraine Wilson-Knox (born May 14, 1973) is an American singer, songwriter, record producer, and actress known for her five-octave coloratura soprano voice. Born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, she was raised by her mother, Crystal Wilson, a singer, and her father, Carl Black, a guitarist; after their divorce in 1979, she moved to Los Angeles with her mother and aunt Penni Wilson. At age nine, she appeared in a commercial with Ella Fitzgerald for Kentucky Fried Chicken. In 1984, she competed on Star Search, the largest national talent show at the time, winning the Junior Vocalist category with performances of "Somewhere Over the Rainbow" and "Greatest Love of All," earning a $5,000 prize. That same year, she joined the cast of Kids Incorporated and performed in the Westwood Playhouse musical Get Happy. John McClain from A&M Records saw her perform and signed her at age eleven. Her debut album, Discovery, released on October 21, 1987, peaked at number 149 on the US Billboard 200; its singles "(Baby Tell Me) Can You Dance" and "No 1/2 Steppin'" became top-ten R&B hits, with the former reaching number fifty on the US Billboard Hot 100. Due to challenges in marketing her as a young artist, she was released from A&M Records. In 1990, she signed with Motown Records and released her second album, Inner Child, internationally on November 19, 1991, which peaked at number eighty-three on the Billboard 200 and number thirteen on the US Top R&B Albums chart. The lead single, "I Love Your Smile," reached number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 and became a number-one hit in several countries, earning a nomination for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 35th Annual Grammy Awards in 1993. The album also produced "I'm Cryin'" (number eleven on the US Hot R&B Singles) and "Silent Prayer" (number thirty-one on the Billboard Hot 100 and number four on the R&B chart), which featured Johnny Gill. Inner Child received a gold certification from the RIAA on May 26, 1992. The single "Saving Forever for You," released on the Beverly Hills, 90210 soundtrack in October 1992, peaked at number four on the US Billboard Hot 100. In July 1993, "It's for You" from The Meteor Man soundtrack reached number fifty-five on the Billboard Hot 100. In June 1994, she released her third album, 21... Ways to Grow, which had initial chart success with "Somewhere" and "Turn Down the Lights" peaking in the top thirty on the US Hot R&B Singles chart, but ultimately became a commercial failure; its final singles "I Like" and "I Wish" had little chart impact. Following the album's poor sales and her release from Motown, she went on a five-year hiatus. During this time, she provided background vocals for several chart-topping songs, including "Un-Break My Heart" and "When You Believe," and contributed to Toni Braxton's Secrets (1996) and Usher's My Way (1997). In January 1997, she made her theater debut as Eponine in the Broadway production of Les Misérables. In 1997, she signed with Arista Records but moved to LaFace Records at the request of co-owner LA Reid. In March 1999, she released her self-titled fourth album on LaFace Records, with the lead single "When I Close My Eyes" moving from number 91 to number 16 on the Billboard Hot 100, peaking at number 12—setting a then-record milestone. Album sales declined after the release of the second single "Yesterday," and in August 1999, she toured as the opening act for NSYNC's Boys of Summer Tour. In 2000, she was dropped from LaFace Records after becoming pregnant with her first child. After appearing in the movie One Special Moment in June 2001, she went on another music hiatus and made a guest appearance in One on One's season one episode "Me & My Shadow." In 2005, she released the single "Every Woman Dreams," which peaked at number 62 on the US R&B chart, and in February 2006, released her fifth studio album Every Woman Dreams on her own record label Imajah Records, which she founded in 2005, named after her children Imani and Elijah. The album peaked at number thirty on the US Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums chart, with singles "Take Care of U" and "So Sexy" reaching within the top seventy on the US Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart. In 2010, she performed vocals on "Behind the Mask" from Michael Jackson's posthumous album Michael and recorded "A Midnight Rendezvous" for the 2012 Kinect game Rhythm Party and "Love Is the Gift" for the video game The Bouncer. In November 2014, the Oprah Winfrey Network aired the reality television series Flex & Shanice, which ran for three seasons and chronicled her life with her husband and their family; to coincide with the show's debut, she released "Gotta Blame Me" and "We Can Fly," followed by "Another Lonely Day in California" in July 2015 and "Breakdown" in 2016. In 2019, she released "He Won't," in 2022 recorded the theme song for the animated children's series Mecha Builders, and in September 2025 starred as former First Lady Michelle Obama in the Off-Broadway production of 44: The Obama Musical. In November 2025, she announced her appearance in the BET+ Christmas movie A Soulful Christmas. Her musical influences include The Emotions, Minnie Riperton, The Clark Sisters, Stevie Wonder, and Teena Marie; she recorded a cover of Riperton's "Lovin' You" on both Inner Child (1991) and Every Woman Dreams (2006) and cited MC Lyte as her favorite rapper, influencing the rap verse on "I Love Your Smile." In November 2018, she launched her beauty line Smile by Shanice, featuring cruelty-free and vegan lipsticks and lip glosses. On February 19, 2000, she married actor and comedian Flex Alexander, with whom she has two children: daughter Imani Knox (2001) and son Elijah Knox (2004). In 2024, she revealed a breast cancer diagnosis and underwent a double mastectomy. Her voice has been described as a coloratura soprano with the ability to sing in falsetto and whistle register. Music critics have noted her strong vocal talent but have also suggested she deserves better songwriting and more creative material. The Grammy Awards, presented annually by the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences, recognize outstanding achievements in music, while the Soul Train Music Awards honor excellence in Black music and entertainment.
